definition: pitchDeg = heel-sole-contact to tail-toe line angle vs floor, + = toe up (brief-literal; includes the static toe-segment offset, so compare against flat-stance baselines within the same construction). Live sole->ankle flatConst/rigidSoleAnkleMm are diagnostics only (the proxy conflates foot pitch with leg swing; corrected 2026-10-18). Clips = (ankle->toe-joint line angle) minus that foot's flat-stance line angle (clip rigidity reported as rigidMm; flat = contact frames with toe within 20 mm of clip floor). Live tail-toe world track stretches up to ~25 mm vs the rigid 120.6 mm clip length, contributing a few deg of uncertainty to heel-tip pitch; ankle interior angle inherits the same caveat. contact = toeY within 0.06 m of foot floor. Planted datum = mean over the contact run preceding liftoff. ankleDeg = interior angle at ankle (knee-ankle-toe), 90 = neutral; dorsiDeg = 90 - ankleDeg. preIC = mean pitch over the 0.2 s (6 live frames) before touchdown.

sources: Atlas of Limb Prosthetics, Chap 13 (Normal Gait): 'Heel strike with the foot at a 25-degree angle to the floor is the normal occurrence' (https://www.oandplibrary.org/alp/chap13-01.asp).

Normative foot-floor-angle study (Gait & Posture, Dec 2018, SciDirect S0958259218300701): FFA at initial contact 18.7+-2.8 deg in 80 typically developing children (4-18 y); band 15-25 covers mean+-1SD (15.9-21.5) and the adult 25-deg value.

ankleDorsiDeg.note: 0 = neutral; + = dorsiflexed. Geometric interior angle band = 85-95 deg.
sources: Atlas of Limb Prosthetics, Chap 13: 'The ankle is in an approximately neutral position (perhaps plantar-flexed 3 degrees)' at initial contact.
ANPT Quick Reference Gait Analysis (2022): initial contact typical joint position 0 deg DF (neutral); terminal swing 'ankle remains in neutral to prepare for initial contact'.
PM&R KnowledgeNow (Biomechanics of Normal Gait): 'Initial Contact ... ankle is at neutral'.
Kaiser 'Normal Gait Mechanics' summary: Initial Contact joint motion 'Ankle Neutral', then plantarflexes 10 deg in loading response.
